title: Yoko Co: Front-End WordPress Developer
description:
Headquarters: McLean, VA
URL: https://www.yokoco.com/
We’re seeking a Front-End Developer who wants to make the world a better place through clean code, thoughtful craftsmanship, and a genuine love of building great websites.
This isn’t just about turning designs into code, it’s about translating ideas into experiences, solving problems along the way, and taking pride in the details that make a site feel right. This role is perfect for someone who enjoys the craft of front-end development, cares about doing things the right way, and is always looking for a better, more efficient way to build.
Why work at Yoko Co?
Do good, better: We exclusively serve clients who make a positive impact on the world. This is your chance to build things that help create a better place for all of us.
4-day flex week and lots of holidays. Mondays are flex days, meaning you’re free to take them off if you’re caught up on your work. Plus, we’re closed for nearly a full week at Thanksgiving (November), and two weeks at the end of the year, plus a bunch of other days, too.
High performance, no jerks. You’ll collaborate with good people who believe in doing great work. Best Place to Work (and that’s not just our opinion).
We’ve been named a Best Place to Work by the Inc. 5000 and Washington Business Journal. We value team members who are motivated by our mission and driven to make a positive impact.
If you have a passion for excellence, a growth mindset, and a commitment to collaboration, we’d love to hear from you.
What you’ll do:
As part of our development team, you’ll build websites and features from design references, turning Figma files into clean, maintainable, production-ready code. Our primary stack is built on Gutenberg block themes, so you’ll spend most of your time there, though you may also work on traditional WordPress themes and, occasionally, other page builders.
Build websites and site features from design references, using industry-standard code and best practices
Develop and maintain WordPress block themes using Gutenberg, templates, parts, patterns, and theme.json configuration
Work with traditional WordPress themes when needed, and occasionally with other page builder platforms
Write clean, well-structured HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Build or extend front-end functionality using React or similar component-based approaches when the project calls for it
Use Git and GitHub for version control, following team branching and code review conventions
Work within a continuous deployment workflow, ensuring changes move smoothly and safely from development to production
Troubleshoot cross-browser and cross-device issues to ensure consistent, polished results
Collaborate with designers, project managers, and strategists to bring projects to life
Look for new and more efficient ways to deliver our work, whether that’s through better tooling, reusable components, or refined processes
Contribute to internal documentation, component libraries, and knowledge sharing
Stay current with WordPress, Gutenberg, and front-end development trends and best practices
What we’re looking for:
We’re less concerned with rigid checklists and more interested in capable, thoughtful developers who care about quality and enjoy solving problems. Strong candidates typically have:
Fluency in WordPress, with experience building both traditional themes and Gutenberg block themes
Comfort working with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript Experience translating design references (Figma or similar) into accurate, responsive, production-ready code
Familiarity with Git workflows and collaborative development practices
Experience working within a continuous deployment or CI/CD pipeline
Experience working with tools like Claude Code, Copilot, or Codex
An eye for detail and a commitment to clean, maintainable code Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Fluent English for written and spoken communication
Bonus points:
Experience building custom Gutenberg blocks
Experience with React or similar component-based frameworks
Experience working in a multi-client or agency environment
You may not want to apply if…
You prefer 100% concrete specs handed to you with no ambiguity and no changes. We do our best to provide final, locked designs and specs, but things inevitably change as a project progresses
You’re not interested in learning or working within Gutenberg block themes
You’d rather work solo than collaborate with designers, PMs, and strategists
You’re reluctant to incorporate AI into your workflow
Front-end development here is a mix of code and configuration, and often requires curiosity, flexibility, and a willingness to find the most efficient path to a great result.
What you get:
You’ll get a flexible schedule, unlimited time off, a competitive salary, a profit share bonus (starting in your second year), the ability to work wherever you want, a personal development budget, and all US federal holidays and multiple weeks off at the end of the year to recharge. We’ll also offset your entire carbon footprint. If you’re in the US, we also offer health insurance, disability and life insurance, and 401(k) matching.
More about us:
We’re a group of people who are passionate about the work we do, the clients we serve, and improving our craft. We also care about each other — we don’t think of one another as coworkers or employees, but as fellow humans. From developers to designers, project managers to strategists, we bring out the best in each other.
We’ve been in business for over a decade, our whole team is remote, and we’ve been named a Best Place to Work by the Inc. 5000 and the Washington Business Journal.
To apply:
If you’re interested, fill out our application form . An actual human from our team looks at every submission. As much as we’d like to, we can’t promise that we’ll reply to every application.
P.S. We encourage you to include a video message!

title: Collibra: Director, Facility Security Officer
description:
Headquarters: Remote, East Coast USA
Joining Collibra Public Sector LLC (CPS)
Collibra Public Sector LLC (CPS) is a DCSA-cleared entity operating under an approved Proxy Agreement (PA) and Affiliated Operations Plan (AOP) as a FOCI-mitigated subsidiary. The Director, Facility Security Officer (FSO) will serve as the principal security advisor to CPS’s Government Security Committee (GSC) and the company's primary interface with the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) and other cognizant security authorities. Additionally, the Director will be responsible for developing, implementing, and ensuring compliance with our Insider Threat Program and be the designated FSO and Insider Threat Security Officer (ITPSO).
This is a foundational leadership role within CPS. The Director will own the ongoing execution and maturation of CPS’s policies in accordance with the National Industrial Security Program. The Director will ensure full compliance with the PA and AOP between CPS and the parent company. The FSO reports to the CPS General Manager and operates under the oversight of the GSC. This role requires independence and a thorough understanding of the obligations that govern FOCI-mitigated entities, facility clearances, and personnel clearances.
The Director, Facility Security Officer is responsible for
FOCI Compliance and Proxy Agreement Execution
Serve as principal advisor to the GSC on all matters related to the PA compliance and any other applicable matters.
Maintain and enforce all obligations under the approved PA and APO, including visit controls, the Electronic Communications Plan, and the Technology Control Plan.
Serve as the primary point of contact with DCSA for all matters related to facility clearances, annual compliance reporting, and all FOCI mitigation oversight.
Review and approve all affiliate contacts, visits and communications between CPS and the parent company in accordance with the approved visit controls procedures.
Develop and maintain a FOCI mitigation instrument (Security Control Agreement, Special Security Agreement, or equivalent) in coordination with outside counsel on FOCI mitigation matters and any open compliance questions.
Establish and maintain all required DSS/DCSA-mandated records, plans, and programs.
Personnel Security
Administer personnel security clearance processing end-to-end via JPAS/DISS, including nominations, investigations, and visit certifications.
Advise employees and managers on clearance eligibility, adjudicative guidelines, and ongoing reporting obligations.
Maintain a current and accurate roster of cleared personnel and access authorizations.
Insider Threat & Security Education
Lead Collibra's Insider Threat Program, including a multi-disciplinary hub and reporting mechanisms.
Develop and deliver annual and ongoing security education and awareness training for cleared and uncleared personnel.
Conduct self-inspection programs and prepare for DCSA facility reviews and annual compliance audits.
Governance & Stakeholder Management
Serve as a trusted advisor to the General Manager and the GSC senior leadership on all security and compliance matters related to the government business.
Partner with independent legal counsel on export control compliance, including ITAR/EAR obligations as they intersect with CPSs products and services.
Support contract compliance and bid activities requiring security documentation or clearance certifications.
Coordinate incident investigations involving potential unauthorized disclosure, fraud, or insider threat, and ensure prompt reporting to GSC and DCSA as required.
You Have
8+ years of experience as a Facility Security Officer or in a substantially similar industrial security role within a cleared defense contractor environment.
Deep working knowledge of the NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), DAAPM/Risk Management Framework, and DCSA oversight processes.
Demonstrated experience managing or supporting FOCI mitigation instruments (PA, Security Control Agreement (SCA), Special Security Agreement (SSA), or equivalent). Experience with proxy-agreement structures specifically is strongly preferred.
Proficiency with JPAS, DISS, and eQIP/SF-86 processing.
Active U.S. Government security clearance (Top Secret required); ability to obtain and maintain clearance at the level required for the role.
Demonstrated ability to operate independently and to enforce compliance boundaries with affiliate and parent company personnel. This role requires someone who is genuinely comfortable saying no when the rules require it.
Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in a FOCI-mitigated environment at a commercial software or technology company, particularly one with active DSCA oversight.
Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot) to solve real-world business challenges, drive measurable outcomes, or streamline workflows.
Familiarity with ITAR/EAR export control compliance as applied to software and SaaS products.
Industrial Security Professional (ISP) or similar certification.
Experience managing COMSEC accounts or working in a multi-facility environment.
You are
A compliance enforcer who leads with credibility, you've built a reputation for holding firm on security boundaries, even when it creates friction with senior stakeholders or affiliate personnel, and you do so with professionalism and clear regulatory grounding.
Independently operating and self-directing, you're comfortable owning a program end-to-end without a security team beneath you, proactively identifying gaps, drafting policies, and driving decisions without waiting for organizational scaffolding to be built around you.
Deeply fluent in FOCI mitigation frameworks, you're familiar with applying Proxy Agreement or Security Control Agreement structures to day-to-day operational decisions, including managing visit controls, affiliate communications, and annual DCSA reporting obligations.
A trusted cross-functional partner, you work naturally alongside legal counsel, General Managers, and executive governance bodies like a GSC, translating dense regulatory requirements into clear guidance that non-security stakeholders can act on.
Familiar with applying export control frameworks to technology products, you understand how ITAR and EAR obligations intersect with software or SaaS environments and can partner with counsel to ensure compliance without blocking the business from operating effectively.
Measures of Success
Within your first month, you will immerse yourself in CPS's existing Proxy Agreement, Affiliated Operations Plan, and all DCSA-mandated records, establish relationships with the Government Security Committee and key stakeholders, and conduct a comprehensive gap assessment of current FOCI compliance posture and personnel security rosters.
Within your third month, you will take full ownership of DCSA communications and annual compliance reporting, implement or strengthen visit controls and the Electronic Communications and Technology Control Plans, and launch a refreshed security education and awareness training program for cleared and uncleared personnel.
Within your sixth month, you will have matured the Insider Threat Program into a fully operational multi-disciplinary hub with established reporting mechanisms, completed a self-inspection cycle in preparation for DCSA facility reviews, and embedded yourself as a trusted advisor to the GSC on all security, ITAR/EAR, and FOCI mitigation matters, setting the long-term compliance foundation for CPS's growth in the public sector.
Compensation for this role
The standard base salary range for this position is $184,000.00 - $230,000.00 per year. This position is not eligible for additional commission-based compensation. Salary offers are based on a combination of factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and location.
In addition to base salary, we offer a competitive total rewards package, including bonus potential, equity for eligible roles, a Flex Fund monthly stipend, pension/401k plans, and more.
Benefits at Collibra
Collibra recognizes and values that everyone has different needs, interests, and life goals. We built our benefits program with flexibility in mind to support you and your loved ones through a diverse range of circumstances and life events. These flexible offerings sit on a foundation of competitive compensation, health coverage, and time off. Learn more about Collibra’s benefits .

More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role
The AI Transformation Owner drives the end-to-end AI agenda for the field organization, translating emerging AI capabilities into concrete enablement roadmaps, field use cases, and org-level strategy. You will partner closely with product and engineering teams to pilot and scale AI solutions, own the operational transformation plan needed to embed AI into day-to-day field workflows, and establish the governance framework that keeps AI adoption safe, compliant, and aligned with company standards. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from strategy to execution without heavy oversight.
This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI.
What You’ll Do
AI Enablement Roadmap: Own and continuously evolve the roadmap for AI-driven enablement initiatives, prioritizing based on field impact, feasibility, and alignment with broader Enterprise AI team and strategy..
AI Field Use Cases: Identify, scope, and execute on high-value AI use cases for the field (e.g., deal support, prospecting, content generation, guided selling, skills, change management), working with stakeholders to define success criteria and measure impact.
AI Field Champions: build relationships with champions in the field organization to activate power-usage and drive peer-led adoption; track this adoption (e.g., usage, proficiency, behavior change) with our AI Ops Specialist and Enablement Analyst.
Ops Transformation Plan: Design and drive the operational plan that turns AI pilots into scaled, repeatable processes, coordinating across enablement, ops, and technical teams to remove execution bottlenecks.
AI Governance: Influence and lead governance standards for AI tool adoption in the field, including data usage, risk review, tool vetting, and alignment with company-wide AI policy.
What You’ll Bring
Mid-Senior Experience: Several years of experience in enablement, sales operations, or a related GTM function, with a track record of owning initiatives end-to-end.
AI Solutions Experience: Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying AI tools or solutions in a business context, with a solid technical understanding of how they work and where they add value. Act as the field's primary advocate for AI tools (e.g., AI-assisted prospecting, call intelligence, forecasting copilots, RFP/proposal generation).
Cross-Functional Fluency: Proven ability to work closely with product and engineering teams, translating field needs into technical requirements and vice versa.
Self-Sufficiency: Comfortable operating with significant autonomy — able to define scope, structure ambiguous problems, and drive work forward without needing detailed direction.
Organization & Execution: Strong project management instincts; able to manage multiple workstreams (roadmap, use cases, ops transformation, governance) in parallel without dropping details.
Innovative Mindset: A builder's orientation toward new technology — curious about what's possible, willing to experiment, and able to separate genuine opportunity from hype.
Enablement/Sales Background: Familiarity with field or sales enablement motions (onboarding, tool adoption, content, coaching) and how AI can realistically augment them.
GitLab Values Alignment: Ability to work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, leaning heavily on transparency and collaboration as defined in the GitLab Handbook.

The Enablement & AI function is part of the CRO organization. Enablement is instrumental in helping GitLab grow at a more accelerated pace and achieve our ambitious revenue targets. title: Service Locator
description:
Building a sustainable tomorrow
KierBAM are a Joint Venture (JV) partnership between Kier and BAM UK & Ireland - BAM UK & Ireland's infrastructure segment is currently delivering the redevelopment project at a Royal Navy site located in Plymouth and we are seeking an experienced Service Locator.
The Service Locator will carry out the physical check and survey of all of the underground services within the area that is being investigated, the Service Locator will have the following responsibilities. You will use various geophysical techniques to locate the service, once they have been found, the services will be marked/spray painted onto the ground in the appropriate colour, defining the type and depth of the service. You will also maintain the contents of the permits on site, making sure the workforce remains compliant with conditions and processes outlined within the permits.
Due to the site being a high-security military naval base, additional security checks will be required a BPSS level of security clearance is necessary. These checks can take up to 8 weeks to process. Only candidates holding EU, NATO, 5 Eyes, or MISWG member passports and who have been UK residents for the last 5 years can be considered for this role. Your team
Location: Devonport Dockyard, Plymouth
Contract: Permanent, 42.5 hours a week Making Possible
In this role as Service Locator, you will be working in a live MOD facility. Your day-to-day tasks will include:
Authorise Permit to Break Surface
Ensure compliance with and enforcement of the project permit for the Break Ground procedure
Review method statements tailored to specific tasks
Mark all services within the work boundaries to protect colour standards
Provide teams with an overview of the services within their designated work boundaries and discuss methods for working around those affected services.
Implement an 8-point checklist during work gang briefings
Enforce any designated exclusion zones surrounding affected services
Obtain the required signatures for permit approval from the works team and the Project Engineer
Notify the BOSC of any discrepancies in the records
Investigate uncharted services as directed by the BOSC
Inform the BOSC of any services that have been removed from the work area, ensuring the service drawings are updated accordingly
Attach the most current SMD CAD drawing to the permit-to-dig
Ensure that no work gang operates under an expired permit for breaking ground or in an area lacking a permit.
Maintain service markings for the duration of the permit as well as incremental scans as excavations progress
This profile is not exhaustive. From time to time, you may be required by the Company to perform other tasks, which are not included in the above description, but are within your capabilities and, where necessary, training, and full support will be given What do you bring to the role?
Essential:
We are seeking a candidate who can handle multiple tasks, show flexibility, and become a key contributor to our team
A CSCS Card is required (this must be obtained before commencing work)
Familiarity with Electromagnetic location and ground penetrating radar is essential
A solid understanding of industry practices and standards related to utility detection, including PAS 128 and TSA, is important
Candidates should have a proficient working knowledge of surveying equipment, such as GPR, CAT, and Genny utility detection tools
The ability to collaborate and communicate effectively within a team and interact with clients on-site is required
Knowledge of HSG-47 and GS-6
Desirable
Experience in the Nuclear environment would be considered beneficial
QCF Level 3 or Level 5 certification in utility mapping is preferred
Applicants should possess a minimum of 2-3 years of utility surveying experience Whats in it for you?
Competitive salary
A wide range of family-friendly policies
Company car/car allowance/travel allowance
8 % matched pension contributions
Private healthcare
Life assurance
26 days holiday
2 wellbeing days
1 volunteering day
Personal and professional development About BAM
Building a sustainable tomorrow. Thats our mission and our promise at BAM. Its how we engineer vital infrastructure and construct high-quality buildings as one of the largest construction companies in Europe.
We strive to create an environment where everybody feels welcome and valued. title: Chief Operating Officer
description:
Description
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the senior operational leader of U.S. Hunger, responsible for translating enterprise strategy into daily execution. This role owns P&L performance across all business lines â Full Cart, Hunger Projects, and the Data/Intelligence engine â ensuring the organization's earned-income model (97%+ of total revenue) operates with precision, accountability, and scalability.
The COO must bring the instincts of an entrepreneur and the discipline of a corporate operator: connecting dots others miss, asking tough questions that drive clarity, and building the systems that allow talented leaders to perform at their highest level. Operational excellence and mission-aligned impact are not in tension here â they are the same thing.
Enterprise Operations & P&L Execution
Own P&L execution across all business lines â each engine must meet its margin, revenue, and impact targets.
Establish and drive the operating cadence â monthly reviews, quarterly business performance reporting, and clear accountability across departments.
Make resource allocation decisions across competing priorities â deploying people, capital, and attention against the highest-value opportunities.
Present operational performance, capacity, and growth execution to the Board of Directors.
Partner with the CEO on scenario planning, structural growth strategies, and enterprise-wide decision-making.
Program Leadership â Full Cart & Hunger Projects
Provide executive oversight of Full Cart and Hunger Projects â ensuring delivery excellence, measurable outcomes, and scalability.
Partner with program directors to evaluate, evolve, and scale programs in response to partner needs, market opportunities, and operational realities.
Drive integration between program design, data infrastructure, and client-facing delivery â ensuring mission impact and revenue execution are operationally connected.
Oversee supply chain and logistics operations to ensure consistent, high-quality program delivery at scale.
Revenue Growth & Partner Execution
Own enterprise revenue execution across health plan partnerships, corporate engagement, and strategic growth opportunities â ensuring acquisition and retention targets are consistently met.
Drive strategies that deepen existing partner relationships and expand engagement across multiple service lines, maximizing long-term value and organizational sustainability.
Represent U.S. Hunger externally with payors, partners, and stakeholders â translating operational insight into compelling value propositions that differentiate USH in the market.
Leverage buyer-side CSR experience and existing relationships across the corporate social impact and food access ecosystem to accelerate partner acquisition and deepen engagement.
Cross-Functional Alignment & Executive Leadership
Partner with the Chief Technology Officer to define business requirements, program design priorities, and operational needs that shape the technology and data roadmap â ensuring platform delivery enables execution across all business lines.
Manage the VP of Finance & Enterprise KPIs and VP of People & Culture â two executives who maintain direct visibility to the CEO through their seat at the executive table â ensuring fiscal discipline, enterprise analytics, and workforce strategy are aligned with operational goals.
Actively contribute to organizational governance, strategy, and enterprise-wide decision-making as the CEO's primary operational counterpart.
Team Leadership & Development
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing operational leadership team â setting clear expectations, driving accountability, and coaching leaders who are growing into executive-level roles.
Develop performance metrics and accountability systems that connect individual and team outcomes to enterprise financial and impact objectives.
Promote a culture of rigorous inquiry, collaboration, and continuous improvement â where leaders are expected to think critically, challenge assumptions, and own their outcomes.
Foster an environment where staff understand both the business drivers of USH's earned-income model and the transformative impact of their work on the communities served.
These essential job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed. Employees will be required to perform other duties as required.
Requirements
10+ years of progressive leadership in operations, business management, or revenue execution â with direct P&L ownership.
Experience building, running, or scaling a business â including sales growth, client retention, and financial performance accountability.
Proven ability to lead and develop directors and VPs â coaching strong operators into executive-level leaders while holding them accountable to outcomes.
Demonstrated pattern of connecting dots across functions â seeing how operational, financial, people, and program decisions impact each other.
Experience at the board level â presenting performance, defending strategy, and engaging C-suite stakeholders directly.
Experience in mission-driven, earned-income environments where market discipline and social impact must coexist.
Strong communication across corporate, nonprofit, healthcare, and community sectors â direct, polished, and confident.
High emotional intelligence, with the courage to ask tough questions, the polish to challenge constructively, and the vision to see what's possible before it's obvious.
Background check is required for this role
Essential Physical Skills
Repetitive finger motion as used in computer use.
Extensive work with computer screens
Everyday requirements of bending, grabbing, holding, and lifting light objects
Work on Hunger Projects requires heavy lifting (up to 50 lbs), moving objects, pushing, and pulling, bending and kneeling
Up to 50% travel time

Manage market expenses responsibly and submit timely documentation.
Work toward clearly defined sales and distribution goals.
Qualifications
Proven experience in sales, brand building, market management, or account management in the New Jersey market.
Existing relationships with New Jersey buyers, distributors, retailers, restaurants, bars, hotels, nightlife venues, or hospitality groups are strongly preferred.
An established book of business is a significant plus.
Demonstrated success opening new accounts and growing existing business.
Experience managing, supporting, and motivating distributor partners.
Strong understanding of the New Jersey wine and spirits market, including its culture, key accounts, and industry landscape.
Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, relationship-management, and organizational skills.
Self-motivated and able to manage a large territory independently.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
Passionate about premium spirits and building a growing brand from the ground up.
Ability to work flexible hours, including occasional nights and weekends, for events, tastings, and activations.
Ability and willingness to travel throughout New Jersey as required.
Valid driverâs license, clean driving record, and reliable transportation.

Commission based on sales performance.
Health, dental, and vision insurance.
Accrued paid time off and sick time.

title: Regional General Manager Airports
description:
Why WestJet
Since our story took off in 1996, WestJet has strived to enrich the lives of everyone in our world; a career with us is no exception. Weâre proud to be one of Canadaâs most admired and respected corporate cultures and continuously aim for the highest standards of service and success.
Join us, this is where your career story takes off.
This position is eligible for remote work, within Canada, under our mobile workforce program.
Regional General Manager, Airports
As the Regional General Manager, you will provide strategic leadership and direction to deliver safe operations while driving excellence in operational performance and guest service through our contracted service partners across the designated region. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Airports, you will lead a team of Regional Managers and collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to maintain regulatory compliance, foster positive relationships, and ensure a consistent, high-quality guest experience across all airport touchpoints within the region.
This role requires an experienced leader who holds service partners accountable for delivering WestJet's operational and service standards while balancing the needs of our guests, our partners, and our business. You will coach and support service partners in developing and executing airport action plans that address performance gaps, strengthen safety, and improve the guest experience.
The Regional General Manager will provide strategic oversight of airport operations across the region by identifying emerging risks, monitoring operational performance, and ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's standards and priorities. Through strong partnerships with service providers and airport authorities, you will drive continuous improvement, enhance operational resilience, and ensure our airports consistently deliver safe, reliable operations and an exceptional guest experience.
Key Deliverables Include
Foster a Safety Above All culture with Regional Managers by ensuring service partners achieve safety targets, monitoring performance trends, and addressing operational risks.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Regional Managers to deliver operational performance, guest satisfaction, employee engagement, and financial results.
Provide strategic oversight of airport operations, ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's operational and guest standards and priorities.
Deliver regional operational performance by achieving operational, guest experience, and financial objectives while driving continuous improvement through station action plans.
Provide governance through audits, operational reviews, and performance assessments to ensure adherence to standards, identify risks, and drive corrective actions.
Analyze operational performance and safety data to identify trends and risks, inform operational decision making, prioritize resources, and strengthen oversight across the region.
Serve as the senior escalation point for Regional Managers, providing leadership and decision support for complex operational, guest, commercial, safety, and irregular operations.
Partner with the Strategic Procurement team to develop service partner strategies, support partner selection, and ensure service partners deliver safe, high-performing, and cost-effective operations.
Build and maintain executive relationships with airport authorities, service partner leadership, government agencies, bargaining agents, and other key stakeholders.
Lead regional operational planning to ensure airports are resourced and operationally ready for seasonal demand, network growth, start-ups, restarts, service partner transitions, station closures, and other strategic initiatives.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by leveraging data and implementing initiatives that enhance operational performance, the guest experience, employee engagement, and financial results.
Participate as a member of the Airports Leadership Team to establish departmental priorities, contribute to strategic direction, and lead the development and execution of departmental initiatives.
Experience And Qualifications
3+ years Airports leadership experience required
Business leadership experience with a significant level of internal and external dependencies and relationships.
Possess strong business acumen to deliver departmental plans including budget.
Proven ability to multitask & handle changing priorities.
Confident in presenting materials and reports to the next 2 levels.
Post-secondary education with a business application an asset.
Ability to manage multiple leaders and locations simultaneously.
Proficient in PC based applications, Microsoft Project, Word, Excel and Outlook.
Ability to travel & spend time away for significant periods of time.
Project management skills considered an asset.
Knowledge of International regulations and guidelines (for example - TSA/Civil Aviation, UK High Commission etc.) an asset.
Proven track record of effectively influencing leadership teams via handling partners and developing strong direct leadership teams.
IATA SGHA experience would be beneficial.
The Benefits Of Being a WestJetter
WestJet provides all WestJetters with a competitive total rewards package. On top of that, we offer:
A fun and friendly culture with colleagues who work together to win
Travel privileges for you and your family, effective from your start date
Savings and Benefit programs that are flexible to meet your specific needs
Think weâre a great fit? Apply now!
About WestJet Group Of Companies
WestJet took to the skies in 1996 with just over 200 employees and three aircraft operating service to five destinations. Since then, WestJet has pioneered low-cost travel in Canada, cutting airfares in half, and increasing the flying population in Canada by more than 50 per cent. Since the Sunwing Airlines integration in 2025, more than 15,000 WestJetters support nearly 200 aircraft and connect guests to our global network of more than 100 destinations across North America, Central America, the Caribbean, Europe and Asia. The WestJet Group is a major Canadian employer and includes WestJet Airlines, WestJet Encore and Sunwing Vacations Group. Weâre Canadaâs leading value airline and largest vacation provider, with a united purpose of providing affordable and accessible air and vacation travel to Canadians.
Our safety promise
At WestJet, the safety and security of our people and our guests is a core value and at the heart of what we do. Safety and security are shared responsibilities all team members are expected to use safe work practices to ensure their well-being and the safety of others. WestJet recognizes that the use of Alcohol and Drugs can adversely impact a safe work environment and the well-being of others including guests, suppliers and the public, as well as place WestJet's operations at risk. All roles that are identified as Safey-Sensitive are required to pass a Pre-Employment Alcohol and Drug Test as per WestJet'sâ¯Alcohol and Drug Policy.â¯
Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion
We embrace what makes each of us unique, and what makes us uniquely WestJet. We welcome diverse skills, experiences and backgrounds so if you're passionate about this role, we encourage you to apply â even if you don't meet every qualification listed. WestJet is committed to inclusiveness, equity and accessibility throughout the selection process. If you require accommodation at any stage, please contact our Talent Acquisition team at talent@westjet.com.

If this role isnât the right fit, we encourage you to explore future opportunities with us.

CASA TRÃS Â· BARCELONA Â· FULL-TIME Â· ON-SITE

A seat in Poble Nou, Barcelona â and a front-row view of productions from the Monaco Grand Prix to the F1 Weekend at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya.

Focal Point Discussion- Ensure this happens between manager, employee & HR and employee is provided feedback with relevant data and developmental inputs.

title: Ship to Shore Technician
description:
Job Description
As a Ship-to-Shore Technician, you will play a vital role in supporting the safe and efficient operation of vessels arriving and departing at the port. This position involves working on the dock to ensure the proper mooring, securing, and release of ships, while maintaining safety and operational standards. In addition to mooring responsibilities, the role will also involve performing general maintenance and support tasks as required to ensure overall port and equipment readiness.
The Ship-to-Shore Technician is responsible for, but not limited to the following:
Docking and Undocking Operations
Assist in safely docking and undocking cruise ships at port using mooring lines, ropes, and related equipment.
Work in coordination with the shipâs captain, crew, and port authorities to ensure that vessels are safely secured and aligned with docking infrastructure.
Mooring Line Management:
Handle and manage mooring lines, ensuring they are properly fastened, tense, and released.
Perform visual inspection of mooring lines and related equipment regularly for wear and damage, ensuring everything is in safe working condition. (Regularly performed by ship crew)
Ship and Dock Safety
Maintain safety protocols during mooring procedures, ensuring that all tasks are performed in accordance with safety regulations.
Monitor weather conditions and report any changes that could affect docking or undocking procedures.
Communication and Coordination
Communicate effectively with other team members on board and shore-based personnel.
Work with the Port Authorities to ensure the timely and safe transfer of passengers and cargo.
Emergency Procedures
Be trained to respond in case of an emergency during docking or undocking operations, including accidents or hazardous situations.
Ensure all mooring operations are conducted efficiently and safely, even under adverse weather conditions or emergencies.
PPE Equipment (MANDATORY)
Must always be in possession of steel toe boots (or prescribed non-slip safety shoes), safety vest, hard hat, gloves, radio/communication device. (To be provided by Carnival)
Cleaning & Maintenance of Pier & Mooring Equipment & Fixtures:
Ensure all mooring equipment such as winches, ropes, and fenders are properly maintained and operational (through visual checks and inspections).
Gangway Inspections & Maintenance: Inspect gangway components for wear, corrosion, proper tension, secure connections, and smooth operation to ensure safe pedestrian access and functionality.
Fenders: Conduct visual inspections of pier fenders and associated hardware to identify cracks, deformation, excessive wear, or damage caused by vessel contact, and report deficiencies as needed.
Mooring Bollards: Regularly inspect mooring bollards for structural integrity, including corrosion, cracks, loose anchor bolts, foundation stress, and coating condition, to ensure safe vessel mooring.
Stanchions & Pier Fixtures: Inspect stanchions and associated components for corrosion, damage, misalignment, or instability, ensuring they remain secure and serviceable.
Ropes: Inspect ropes for wear, fraying, or damage, and verify they are properly positioned and suitable for continued use.
Mooring Equipment Maintenance: Perform minor maintenance and repairs of mooring equipment when necessary.
Pier & Dock Cleaning: Maintain clean, safe, and non-slip pier surfaces by removing dirt, salt, algae, stains, debris and other buildup by pressure washing and using prescribed cleaning equipment and solutions, along all designated cruise pier and trestle areas.
Cleaning Equipment Operation: Safely inspect, operate, and maintain cleaning equipment, including scrubbers and pressure washers, ensuring proper use, cleaning, and storage after each operation.
Additional Maintenance Support Activities
Perform minor maintenance support to technical teams including plumbing, electrical, masonry, carpentry, and HVAC functions.
Mandatory Training:
Maintain compliance with organizational requirements by attending and participating in all required company training sessions.
Lagoon Care
Perform maintenance/inspections of lagoon systems.
Education:
Education: High School Diploma.
Maintenance knowledge is preferred.
Certified Pool Operator (CPO) required within 6 months of employment start.
Three to Five years' experience working in a mooring or associated fields.
Essential Experience Required:
Must be physically fit. Must have strong customer service skills. Ability to work in an outdoor environment. Ability to multi-task and think critically. Previous work experience preferred. Prolonged periods standing and working outside. Must be able to lift, up to 50 pounds at times. All island employees must be physically able to participate in emergency lifesaving procedures and drills. Full use/range of motion of arms and legs as well as full visual, verbal and hearing abilities are required to receive and give instructions in the event of an emergency. Ability to read and write English to understand and interpret written procedures. This includes the ability to give and receive instructions in written and verbal forms and to effectively present information and respond to questions from guests, managers, and co-workers.

title: Program & Events Coordinator
description:
About the LSPA: The LSP Association (LSPA) is a non-profit association for Massachusetts Licensed Site Professionals (LSPs) and other related environmental practitioners who work on behalf of property owners, operators, and other involved parties to assess and cleanup oil and hazardous materials (OHM) released to the environment. LSPs are licensed by the Commonwealth to oversee this work and, since 1993, over 40,000 contaminated properties have been brought into regulatory compliance.
The LSPA's mission is to support our membership in achieving and maintaining a high standard of practice in the assessment and remediation of contaminated sites in Massachusetts and New England. The LSPA provides technical and educational resources to our membership in the form of programming, networking events, committees, and resources. The LSPA also serves as an advocate to the profession with MassDEP, the LSP Board of Registration, and the state legislature, and as a resource to the public.
Job Description: The Program & Events Coordinator plays a critical role in the success of the LSPA and serves as a primary point of contact for our members, volunteers, and sponsors. This individual is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing the association's educational programs and networking events, administering the sponsorship program, and providing customer service support. Success in this position means delivering high-quality member experiences, maintaining strong relationships with volunteers and sponsors, and ensuring the smooth administration of our continuing education program.
The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously. This individual enjoys working independently while collaborating closely with volunteers, board members, speakers, sponsors, and staff.
Key Responsibilities:
Educational Programs : Coordinate, plan, and manage programs and speakers for all LSPA courses, membership meetings, emerging professional events, the Annual Fall Party, and the Environmental Symposium. The LSPA hosts one to three events per month with 25-250 people in attendance. Approximately 65% of programming is hosted virtually. Content creation is performed in conjunction with input from the Executive Director, Committee Chairs, Education Committee, and Board of Directors.
Event Logistics: For in-person events, source event venues and help facilitate contracts; plan food and beverage, room set-up, and audiovisual needs; reconcile venue bills; and serve as the point of contact on-site. For virtual programs, setup and run the virtual meeting platform, monitor attendance and engagement, create moderator scripts and slides, and train speakers on how to use the virtual platform.
Continuing Education (CE) Administration : Compile CE materials for all educational courses and meetings; submit materials for credit approval with the LSP Board of Registration, the Connecticut Licensed Environmental Professional (LEP) Board, and other Boards/entities; maintain CE records related to attendance, engagement, and evaluation; issue certificates of attendance to attendees; and attend monthly virtual LSP Board of Registration meetings.
Sponsorship : Help administer the corporate and event sponsorship program, including updating the sponsorship prospectus, facilitating invoices/payments, maintaining contact lists, conducting outreach, and working with sponsors to access their sponsorship benefits.
Member Service and Organizational Support : Help monitor and respond to inquiries received through the organization email inbox; provide customer service to members, sponsors, speakers, and event attendees; attend Board meetings, leadership meetings, and committee meetings as requested; and support association operations and special projects as needed.
Qualifications
The person hired for this role should have the following qualifications:
Experience:
2-5 years of experience in program/event planning, project management, or another related field.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and proven ability to provide excellent customer service.
Strong project management skills with excellent attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines independently.
Comfortable coordinating, building relationships with, and communicating professionally with members, volunteers, sponsors, vendors, and other external stakeholders/partners.
Technology:
Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Zoom Meetings and Zoom Webinar, including coordinating presenters from multiple locations, incorporating polling, and managing technical issues.
Association management systems (AMS) or member databases.
Online registration and evaluation platforms.
Canva or similar design tools (preferred, not required).
Preferred Qualifications (not required):
Experience working for a nonprofit organization, professional association, or membership-based organization.
Experience with the environmental sciences industry.
Familiarity with sponsorship development or relationship management.
Bachelor's degree, Associate's degree with relevant experience, or significant relevant professional experience demonstrating the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the position successfully.
Why Join the LSPA?
This is an opportunity to work with a respected association that supports environmental professionals making a meaningful impact on public health and environmental protection throughout Massachusetts and New England. As a small organization, we offer autonomy, flexibility, and the opportunity to build relationships with industry leaders while helping shape the educational and professional development experiences of our members. Compensation and benefits include:
Salary : The salary range for this position is $70,000â$80,000 annually. Compensation will be based on a variety of factors such as individual qualifications and experience.
Benefits : LSPA employees receive $300 per month for a Healthcare Reimbursement Account (HRA) that may be used to reimburse certain medical and insurance-related expenses. The organization does not currently offer group health or dental insurance plans. In addition, employees have access to a 401(k) plan.
PTO : 15 days of paid time off (PTO) annually for the first three years (increases to 20 days thereafter). The LSPA also provides 14 holidays per year (inclusive of 5 floating holidays).
Fully remote position : Candidates may reside anywhere in New England, with preference given to Massachusetts-based applicants. Travel to Massachusetts-based programs and events approximately 10â12 times annually is required.
Reimbursement for home office expenses : $750 annually.
How to Apply
Please submit a cover letter and resume to mmorris@lspa.org. Applications without cover letters or that request compensation/benefits beyond what we can provide will not be reviewed.
The LSPA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, contact mmorris@lspa.org.
The LSPA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

title: Chief of Staff the CEO
description:
The job in one line
You run the CEO's operating system: goals, cadence, and follow-through. You also personally own the projects that don't have a home yet.
Everyday Dose is moving fast in a lot of directions at once. The constraint isn't ideas or effort. It's making sure the right handful of things get set, tracked, and actually finished while everything else keeps running.
That's this job. It is not an executive assistant role and it is not a note-taking role. You'll own outcomes, run the meeting the leadership team is accountable to, and have a real seat.
What You'll Actually Do
Own goal setting. Run quarterly and annual planning end to end. Sit with each exec, turn intent into targets that are measurable and few. Hold the line when a goal is a paragraph instead of a number. Publish it so the whole company knows what we're playing for.
Manage against those goals. Goals decay the week after they're written unless someone owns them. You're that someone. You track progress, surface slippage early, and escalate the things that need the CEO before they become fires.
Run the weekly leadership meeting. Set the agenda, bring the numbers, drive to decisions. Every meeting ends with owners and dates, and you chase them down between meetings. You're not the scribe; you're the person who makes the hour worth everyone's time.
Keep the scoreboard honest. Build and maintain the company-level reporting leadership runs on, in partnership with finance and data. Numbers come from the warehouse, not from someone's recollection on a call. If two sources disagree, you're the one who reconciles them.
Run special projects. The high-stakes, cross-functional thing that has no owner: a new bet, a partnership, a channel or business we're deciding whether to enter, a problem that spans three teams and belongs to none of them. You get handed ambiguity and come back with an answer, a model, and a plan.
Be the CEO's second read. Pressure-test decisions before they're made. Prep board and investor materials. Write the memo when the thinking needs to be sharp. Say the thing nobody else in the room will say.
What Success Looks Like In 90 Days
Company goals for the quarter are written, owned, and measurable, and every leader can recite theirs without opening a doc
The weekly leadership meeting has a repeatable format, a live scoreboard, and decisions that stick
One company-level dashboard everyone trusts, sourced from the warehouse
Two special projects taken from ambiguous to finished without supervision
The CEO's time visibly reallocated toward the highest-leverage work in the business
Requirements
What we're looking for
8 to 12 years of experience, including time as a Chief of Staff, BizOps lead, Strategy & Operations lead, or equivalent to a founder/CEO or a senior exec
Top pedigree. Strong academic background and time at companies with a known high bar, plus a record of being promoted inside them. We look hard at both
Left brain. You're fluent in a spreadsheet and comfortable in a data environment. You can build a model, size an opportunity, read a cohort curve, and pull your own numbers rather than filing a ticket and waiting
Right brain. You write exceptionally well. Memos, board decks, exec comms. You can take a messy 90-minute discussion and turn it into one page that changes what people do
You've run an operating cadence (OKRs or equivalent, weekly business reviews, planning cycles) at a company doing real volume, not as a theory from a deck
Backbone. You will regularly tell senior, accomplished people that their goal isn't measurable or their project is late. You do it without drama and without flinching, and they respect you for it
Startup metabolism. High ambiguity, fast context switching, nothing beneath you. You'd rather own the outcome than protect the org chart
You use AI tooling daily to move faster on analysis, drafting, and research
Bonus
DTC, subscription, or CPG experience, especially a business with recurring revenue and real retention mechanics
Consulting, banking, or PE foundation plus real operating experience (we're not looking for one without the other)
You've built materials for and presented to a board or investors
SQL, or enough of it to be dangerous
What this role is not
Not an executive assistant. You are not managing a calendar or booking travel
Not a project manager who takes notes and updates a tracker
Not a strategy role that stops at the recommendation
Not a functional leadership role. You won't inherit a team on day one, though this role can grow into one
If you want a clear lane and a stable scope, this isn't it, and that's fine.
How To Apply
Skip the cover letter. Instead, send us:
One page on an operating cadence you built or ran. What existed before, what you changed, and what measurably improved as a result
A time you told an executive something they didn't want to hear. What you said, and what happened
Short answer: A subscription business is seeing retention slip. Five executives each have a confident, different theory as to why. You have two weeks. What do you look at first, how do you get to the actual answer, and how do you land it with a leadership team that's already made up its mind?
We read these carefully. Applications without them won't move forward.
Benefits
Strong base, performance bonus
Meaningful equity because we want you to own a piece of what you build
Health benefits + health stipend
Generous time off
Free product

description:
Oula delivers maternity care built around our patientsâoffering comprehensive support before, during, and after pregnancy. With fewer C-sections and higher VBAC success rates, our research-backed approach is delivering better outcomes. Our team of trusted midwives, OBGYNs, and dedicated care navigators ensure our patients get the type of care they need in the moments that matter most.
Since launching in 2021, weâve expanded to include Preconception and Miscarriage Care, Pregnancy Care, Postpartum Support, and Gynecology. We currently have 4 clinics in the tri-state area, with three new clinics opening in 2026! Come join our team of clinicians, innovators, operators, and technologists passionate about setting a new standard in maternity care.
OULA HEALTH
Product Manager
Full-Time
New York, Chicago or Charlotte
Reports to VP, Central Operations
About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems â including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health â to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.
The Role
At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR â it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack â including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver. You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert â FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations â standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable â documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout
What You Bring
3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work â ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity â you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines â ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak âmultiple languagesâ â comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.
Compensation & Details
Salary: $110,000 â $140,000 depending on experience and location
Equity: Options commensurate with level
Location: Preference for New York/New Jersey/Connecticut, Chicago or Charlotte Remote-flexible with periodic travel to clinic locations and health system partners
Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision; 401(k); generous PTO
Oula offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, and comprehensive benefits. Exact compensation inclusive of salary and any bonuses is determined based on a number of factors including experience and skill level, location, and qualifications which are assessed during the interview process. Oula is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone's contributions are valued.
Salary Range: $110,000 USD - $140,000 USD
Oula's Commitment as an Equal Opportunity Employer :
We want you to know: You can be a great candidate even if you don't fit everything we've described above. You can also have important skills we haven't thought of. If that's you, don't hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself (especially in your cover letter â this is where you can really state your case for *why you*). We are committed to fostering diversity in our organization and building an equitable and inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and experiences. We're taking steps to meet that commitment. We especially encourage members of traditionally underrepresented communities to apply, including women, people of color, LGBTQ people, veterans, and people with disabilities.

title: Video Editor Reacts
description:
About Us
Beast Industries is a multifaceted media and entertainment company founded by Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, the most watched person in the world. Renowned for revolutionizing digital content creation, Beast Industries encompasses a diverse portfolio of ventures that extend far beyond its origins on YouTube. With a mission to entertain, inspire, and create significant social impact, Beast Industries operates across various domains including digital media, philanthropy, consumer products, and innovative business initiatives. At Beast Industries, we believe in the transformative power of digital media and its potential to entertain, educate, and effect positive change. Our commitment to innovation, creativity, and philanthropy drives us to explore new frontiers, create unforgettable experiences, and build a legacy that inspires future generations. About the Role
MrBeast is looking for a data-driven, creative, and fast-paced Video Editor to join our Content & Post-Production team working on the MrBeast Reacts channel. This role is for a master-level editor who lives and breathes YouTube culture, capable of transforming raw multi-cam reaction feeds into hyper-engaging content that keeps millions of viewers locked in. You will thrive in a high-feedback environment, balancing aggressive production schedules with a relentless obsession for frame-by-frame pacing and audience retention. What You'll Do
Cut and assemble raw multi-cam reaction footage, seamlessly balancing primary talent commentary, PIP source media, and visual punch-ins.
Engineer high-retention video intros and hooks that immediately fulfill title and thumbnail promises within the first 30 seconds.
Execute hyper-fast pacing, comedic timing, and visual pop-ups, including kinetic typography, memes, and custom tracking graphics.
Perform high-quality sound design, including impactful SFX, dynamic music ducking, and precise audio balancing for voice clarity.
Collaborate closely with Lead Editors and creative teams to incorporate rapid turnaround notes and feedback loops.
Analyze YouTube retention curves alongside lead editors to pinpoint drop-off moments and refine pacing rules for subsequent edits.
Maintain clean, highly organized timeline projects in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects, adhering to internal post-production standards.
Coordinate with the thumbnail team to ensure visual assets and key video climaxes align perfectly with channel creative strategy.
Stay ahead of internet culture and viral editing meta to continuously inject fresh humor and visual variety into channel content. What We're Looking For
3+ years of professional video editing experience focused on high-pacing YouTube, commentary, or viral digital content.
Expert-level proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and Adobe After Effects, specifically with keyframing, motion tracking, masking, and dynamic linking.
Deep structural understanding of YouTube algorithm dynamics, Average View Duration (AVD), CTR, and retention curve analysis.
Mastery of dynamic sound design, audio leveling, and music curation to enhance comedic and emotional shifts.
A data-driven mindset that prioritizes viewer retention evidence over personal creative assumptions.
High feedback sensitivity, with the ability to handle rapid creative criticism constructively and pivot quickly.
Exceptional attention to detail, maintaining frame-by-frame precision in pacing and visual overlays.
Proven ability to manage high-volume workflows, including file compression, color correction, and final exports optimized for YouTube.
Extreme ownership over end-to-end video performance, production deadlines, and technical accuracy. Benefits The Perks, Why Work On the MrBeast Team
We are redefining what entertainment and storytelling look like at global scale. Every piece of content we publish reaches millions and influences culture in real time. This is your opportunity to lead the team that decides how those moments come to life across every screen.
Competitive Salary
Generous Medical (Blue Cross Blue Shield), Dental, Vision and company-paid Life InsuranceÂ
Company contributions to employee Health Savings Accounts (HSA)Â
401k Plan with Safe Harbor company-matching
Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays
Company-provided technology packageÂ
Relocation assistance where applicable, including travel and company-provided housing for the first 90 days

title: Area Sales Manager
description:
Job Title:
Area Sales Manager
Reports to:
Director of Sales- East
Location:
Remote- New York Metro
Status:
FT/Exempt
Compensation:
$70,000 â $80,000 annual base salary, plus a competitive bonus opportunity. Final compensation will be commensurate with experience, skills, and qualifications.
ABOUT THE COMPANY
ROAR is redefining hydration for a new generation. In a category that has become overly serious and hardcore performance obsessed, ROAR stands for something different: hydration that is expressive, effortless, and rooted in real life. Built for people who move, connect, and live life out loud, ROAR delivers complete hydration with vitamins, antioxidants, and electrolytes - all with just 20 calories and 3g of sugar or less per bottle.
More than a beverage, ROAR is a cultural signal - bright, approachable, and fun. It rejects the intensity and rules of traditional hydration in favor of something more human: joy, spontaneity, and the kind of movement that doesnât need a scoreboard. This positioning has resonated with consumers and retailers alike driving strong momentum across both natural and conventional retail, where ROAR continues to expand rapidly and now ranks as the #2 brand in the natural channel within the enhanced water category.
ROLE OVERVIEW
ROAR Organic is seeking a hands-on Sales Leader to drive profitable growth in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. This role is responsible for leading all sales activities across grocery customers in the New York Metro area, including new business development, key account management, and executing data-driven strategies to expand market share and increase brand awareness.
The ideal candidate brings a proven track record of scaling high-growth brands profitably, with experience managing both established and emerging grocery retailers, as well as partners. They are highly relationship-driven, resourceful, and action-oriented, with strong communication and organizational skills. This leader excels at building and implementing the strategies, tools, and processes needed to support sustained growth.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Deliver against Annual Operating Plan targets, including gross/net sales and trade spend objectives.
Grow distribution and topline revenue with a focus on regional and independent retailers.
Execute customer sales strategies, promotional calendars, and account plans.
Leverage distributer incentive programs and independent retailer promotional opportunities to drive sales.
Conduct weekly route rides with distributor sales representatives to support execution and identify growth opportunities.
Develop and own a field execution strategy based on weekly trend reports, promotional planners, and merchandising opportunities.
Manage and execute trade spend programs to drive profitable growth and promotional effectiveness.
Leverage syndicated data (IRI, SPINS) to communicate compelling, retailer-specific presentations.
Track, measure, and analyze performance metrics, including ROI.
Represent the brand at regional and national trade shows, customer meetings, and industry events.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
Minimum 2 years of CPG sales experience.
Strong understanding of the beverage and grocery landscape, including retailers and distributors.
Experience executing sales planning initiatives.
Creative, solutions-oriented problem solver with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
Thrives in a hands-on, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
Proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with syndicated data tools (SPINS, IRI) preferred.
Ability to travel extensively as needed.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
Ability to lift up to 30 pounds.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship.
